newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek rates frozen, bonds lose ground, ecu/drs up.
newsitem.headline: Greek rates frozen, bonds lose ground, ecu/drs up.

text.p: Greece's interbank depos and forex forwards were consolidating in late quiet dealings, fixed coupon bonds were softer and the drachma was weaker against the ecu, dealers said.
"Depos and forex forwards are stable, holding morning levels," said a dealer at a foreign bank. "I guess the market took its cue from the central bank's move to leave liquidity unchanged."

The Bank of Greece drained 100 billion drachmas of 14-day funds at 11.90 percent in its regular fixed rate tender on Wednesday. A 14-day pact of 100 billion drachmas expired today so that net liquidity was left intact.

Some traders said they expected interest rates to ease from current levels but others pointed out that light selling of bonds from foreign players and a liquidity squeeze from the forex formed a floor for drachma interbank rates at current levels.

Selling of fixed coupon bonds pushed yields a few ticks higher to 9.20 percent for the 10-year bond, 9.90 percent for the seven-year paper, 9.75 percent for the five-year bond and 10.10 percent for the three-year bond.
"Yields have risen slightly on some selling of fixed coupons from foreign players," a bond dealer said.
The mark was quoted at 157.53/63 from Wednesday's 157.640 fix, the dollar at 274.95/05 drachmas from 275.070 and the ecu at 309.60/70 from 309.66 drachmas.

"Ecu/drahma is hovering around 309.60/70," said a forex trader at a foreign bank. "It hit 309.70/75 earlier on mark and ecu buying from a large state bank but has eased thereafter. The market is thin and can go either way even when small amounts are involved."

High interbank rates and a stronger U.S. dollar shielded the drachma from persistent selling pressure that could have emerged on the back of turbulence in other foreign exchange markets, a senior dealer ata private bank said.
